5 things every invoice needs
tips: An invoice number: So you and the client can find it fast.
A real due date: A date, not "ASAP" or "when you can".
What you did, line by line: Clear items are easier to approve.
How to pay you: Bank details or a payment link.
Your payment terms: Late fee or deposit rules, if you have them.

Batch a week of content in one afternoon
tips: Pick 3 topics: One idea per post, nothing more.
Write all the hooks first: The first line decides if people stay.
Film everything in one go: Same light, same outfit, less setup.
Edit and schedule next day: Fresh eyes catch the boring parts.

How to chase a late invoice politely
tips: Day 1 late: friendly reminder: Short, kind, invoice attached.
Day 7: second reminder: Ask if anything is blocking payment.
Day 21: final notice: Give one clear date to pay by.
Wait a few days between emails: Log each reminder so you don't spam.

Make more of the winner: Keep the others as support.

Ask this before you quote a project
tips: What does "done" look like?: Get the finish line in writing.
What's the deadline?: Rush work costs more. Say so.
How many feedback rounds?: Unlimited changes = unlimited work.
What's the budget range?: Saves you both a wasted proposal.
Who approves the work?: One decision maker, fewer surprises.

5 hook ideas to steal for your next post
tips: "Stop doing X if you want Y": Calls out a common mistake.
"I tried X for 30 days": People want to know how it ended.
"3 mistakes I made with X": Honest and easy to relate to.
"How I do X in 10 minutes": Promises a fast, clear result.
"Nobody tells you this about X": Makes people curious.

How to ask for a deposit without the awkward
tips: Put it in the proposal: Not as a surprise after they say yes.
Ask 30 to 50% upfront: Enough to protect your time.
Start when it's paid: The deposit is the real "yes".
Split big jobs into milestones: Get paid as each part is done.

Newsletter: Write the story behind it.

Find your real hourly rate
tips: Count every hour: Calls, emails and fixes count too.
Subtract project costs: Tools, fonts, stock photos, travel.
Divide what's left by hours: That's what you really earned per hour.
Compare it to your quote: Too low? Raise prices or cut extras.

Check this before you post
tips: Hook in the first second: Say the point right away.
Captions on screen: Many people watch with sound off.
A clear cover: Readable title, even when small.
A question in the caption: Gives people a reason to comment.
Keywords, not just hashtags: Write what people would search.

A proposal that wins has these 5 parts
tips: Their problem first: Show you listened before you sell.
2 or 3 options: Let them choose, not just say yes or no.
Clear price and timeline: No "it depends" on the page.
An expiry date: A gentle reason to decide this week.
One next step: "Reply yes and I'll send the invoice."

How to pitch a brand in 5 lines
tips: Pick brands you already use: Your pitch sounds real because it is.
Say who your audience is: Who they are, not just how many.
Share real past results: Only true numbers, or none at all.
Give one clear idea: "A 30-second tutorial using X."
Keep it short: Easy to read means easy to answer.

Deposit paid: Then the work begins.

tips: Write the scope down: Before the work starts.
Name the extra: "That's outside what we agreed."
Offer a price for it: Extra work, extra invoice.
Or swap it: "We can do this instead of that."

Get paid by brands on time
tips: Agree on fee and posts in writing: Even a short email counts.
Ask for the payment date: "Net 30" means 30 days. Write it down.

Follow up the day it's late: Polite, short, invoice attached.
